gen-gf-wallpoet-gf-kiwi-maru: Commanding in a stencil-cut way, Wallpoet rises tall and leaves thin gaps of paper between its letters. Yet Kiwi Maru, a text serif, spreads out generously with round o's, so a long page unfolds at a gentler, more traditional pace.
gen-gf-wallpoet-gf-padyakke-expanded-one: Bold lettering with tall lowercase opens this pair, Wallpoet cutting sharp, smooth curves with gaps between its strokes. But Padyakke Expanded One is a wide, literary serif with a line you can trace, and it would feel sprawling if the heading were shrunk down to match.
gen-gf-wallpoet-gf-stint-ultra-expanded: Bold and brash, Wallpoet stands tall with slim cracks of daylight running through its letters. Stint Ultra Expanded, a text serif, lets each character float apart in an unvarying line, so the two trade a stencil punch for a stretched-out, traditional hush.
gen-gf-walter-turncoat-fs-bespoke-slab: Walter Turncoat writes in tubular, neon-glass strokes with a tall middle band and shallow ascenders, relaxed and a bit casual. Bespoke Slab is a grounded serif with tall bodies, and it isn't meant for long paragraphs.
gen-gf-walter-turncoat-fs-familjen-grote: Familjen Grotesk is a lively sans with tall lowercase and bowls left open on one side, made for short stretches of reading. Walter Turncoat, cut like strips of equal width, would look lost if the heading were made small.
gen-gf-walter-turncoat-fs-hind: Relaxed, hand-drawn letters in tubular strokes lead here, with shallow ascenders and a tall middle band. Hind follows as a plain sans whose lowercase nearly matches its capitals, steady and better for brief copy than anything longer.
gen-gf-walter-turncoat-fs-hoover: Relaxed and pen-and-paper casual, Walter Turncoat draws every diagonal as stout as every upright in its copper-pipe strokes. But Hoover, a classic serif with compressed ascenders and a generous e, is the one made for short stretches of reading.
gen-gf-walter-turncoat-fs-pilcrow-rounde: Pilcrow Rounded reads warm and tight, with big counters, tall lowercase and curves that refuse to close, good for a handful of lines. And Walter Turncoat does the loose, handwritten flourish best, while the body font keeps its sans-serif letters snug and tidy.
gen-gf-walter-turncoat-fs-technor: Technor reads cool and geometric, its neon-tube letters glowing with one line thickness and barely any gap between cases. Walter Turncoat's handwriting loosens that precision, and the sans is made for short stretches of reading.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-bhutuka-expanded-one: Ink strokes that taper out before they touch give Warnes its expressive, spacious look, with no stroke contrast at all. BhuTuka Expanded One, a classic serif, slows a longer passage to a leisurely walk, its curvy letters feeling unclamped.
